intro: Hamburg rewards visitors with lively docks, elegant lakes and a famously creative nightlife. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: S-Bahn and U-Bahn cover the city; no trams since the 1970s.
Buy tickets before boarding buses; no ticket sales on board.
Single tickets run about €2.10-12.60; day tickets from €8.20.
Ride apps like Uber and Bolt work; taxis are metered and plentiful.
Driving is slow with roadworks and costly parking; use park-and-ride.
The city is flat and good for cycling; ferries cross the Elbe.

miniatur_wunderland.name: Miniatur Wunderland
miniatur_wunderland.price_text: ≈ €25 adults · cheaper for children · book a time slot online
miniatur_wunderland.hours: Daily, roughly 08:00/09:00–19:00 or later; check on the day
miniatur_wunderland.tip: Book a timed ticket online well ahead. Weekday mornings are quietest.

elbphilharmonie.name: Elbphilharmonie
elbphilharmonie.hours: Plaza daily, roughly 09:00–24:00; check on the day
elbphilharmonie.tip: Get a free or low-cost plaza ticket online for the outdoor deck and its harbour view.

speicherstadt.name: Speicherstadt
speicherstadt.tip: Walk the brick canals at dusk when the warehouses light up. It is a UNESCO area.

hafencity.name: HafenCity
hafencity.tip: Combine the waterfront walk with the Elbphilharmonie and Speicherstadt in one loop.

reeperbahn.name: Reeperbahn
reeperbahn.price_text: Free to walk · drinks and shows extra
reeperbahn.hours: Busiest at night; some venues late
reeperbahn.tip: Walk it once in daylight to see the street, then again after dark for the atmosphere. Stay on the main street late at night.

st_michaelis.name: St. Michael's Church, Hamburg
st_michaelis.price_text: ≈ €8 tower climb; church entry free or small donation
st_michaelis.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–18:00; check on the day
st_michaelis.tip: Climb the tower for the best city view. The lift is handy if stairs are too much.

elbe_river.name: Elbe River
elbe_river.tip: Sit on the Elbe beach steps near Övelgönne at sunset and watch the ships pass.

fish_market.name: Fish Market Hamburg
fish_market.price_text: Free entry · food and drink paid separately
fish_market.hours: Sunday mornings only, roughly 05:00–09:30; check on the day
fish_market.tip: Go early on Sunday. The fish rolls and the auction hall atmosphere are the draw.

tropen_aquarium.name: Hagenbeck Tropen-Aquarium
tropen_aquarium.price_text: ≈ €25 adults · combo tickets with the zoo available
tropen_aquarium.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–18:00; check on the day
tropen_aquarium.tip: Buy a combined zoo and aquarium ticket online to save time at the gate.

rathaus.name: Hamburg City Hall
rathaus.price_text: Free to view the square · guided tours small fee
rathaus.hours: Building exterior always visible; tours on set days, check on the day
rathaus.tip: Look at the facade from the Rathausmarkt, then join a short guided tour if one runs.

harbor_boat_tour.name: Hamburg Harbor Boat Tour
harbor_boat_tour.price_text: ≈ €15–25 for a 1-hour tour; check on the day
harbor_boat_tour.tip: Take a one-hour tour from the Landungsbrücken piers. Sit outside for the best views.

volksparkstadion.name: Volksparkstadion
volksparkstadion.price_text: Match tickets vary widely; check on the day
volksparkstadion.hours: Match days only for most visitors
volksparkstadion.tip: Only worth a trip if you have a match ticket. Check the fixture list before planning.

wanderer.name: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
wanderer.landmark: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
wanderer.price_text: Free to view in the Kunsthalle collection; check current display
wanderer.hours: Museum hours vary; check on the day
wanderer.tip: This Caspar David Friedrich painting is in the Hamburger Kunsthalle. Confirm it is on display before you go.

wildpark.name: Wildpark Schwarze Berge
wildpark.price_text: ≈ €10 adults · cheaper for children; check on the day
wildpark.hours: Daily, roughly 08:00–18:00; check on the day
wildpark.tip: A half-day trip south of the city for families. Bring sturdy shoes for the woodland paths.

landungsbruecken.name: Landungsbrücken piers
landungsbruecken.tip: The classic harbour viewpoint. Walk the covered pier and watch the ferries come in.

schanzenviertel.name: Schanzenviertel walk
schanzenviertel.price_text: Free to walk · cafés and bars extra
schanzenviertel.hours: Always open; liveliest afternoon and evening
schanzenviertel.tip: Wander the side streets for street art, cafés and small shops. It is a good contrast to the harbour.

fischmarkt_food.name: Fischmarkt food stalls
fischmarkt_food.hours: Sunday mornings only; check on the day
fischmarkt_food.tip: Try a fish roll and a coffee. Bring cash for the smaller stalls.

planten_un_blomen.name: Planten un Blomen
planten_un_blomen.hours: Daily, roughly 07:00–22:00; check on the day
planten_un_blomen.tip: A calm green break near the centre. The water-light shows in summer evenings are free.

oewelgoenne.name: Övelgönne Elbe beach
oewelgoenne.tip: A small sandy river beach with a view of passing ships. Good for a relaxed sunset walk.

dialogue_im_dunkeln.name: Dialog im Dunkeln
dialogue_im_dunkeln.hours: Set tour times; check on the day
dialogue_im_dunkeln.tip: A guided tour in complete darkness led by blind guides. Book a slot in advance.

grosse_freiheit.name: Große Freiheit and Beatles Platz
grosse_freiheit.tip: See the Beatles sculptures and the small clubs where the band played early on.

alter_elbtunnel.name: Alter Elbtunnel
alter_elbtunnel.tip: Walk or cycle the old tunnel under the Elbe. It is a quick, free and unusual experience.

karolinenviertel.name: Karolinenviertel walk
karolinenviertel.hours: Always open; best in the afternoon
karolinenviertel.tip: Small shops, flea markets and food spots near the Messe. A good low-key neighbourhood stroll.

stays.why: Central for the Rathaus, Kunsthalle and the lake. Walk to the main station and U/S-Bahn.
Next to the Elbphilharmonie and Speicherstadt. New hotels, quiet nights, short walk to the water.
Nightlife, the Reeperbahn and the harbour edge. Lively and loud on weekends.
Local feel, good food, river views from the Elbe beach. Quick S-Bahn ride to the centre.

food: Try a Fischbrötchen (fish sandwich) at the Landungsbrücken or the fish market; prices are roughly €4–8.
Franzbrötchen is the local cinnamon pastry. Buy one warm from a bakery for about €2–3.
Labskaus and Grünkohl are classic Hamburg dishes; look for them on traditional restaurant menus.
The Sunday fish market in Altona (early morning) is a Hamburg ritual; check opening hours on the day.
Book ahead for dinner on the Reeperbahn or in HafenCity on weekends; walk-ins get harder after 19:00.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a harbour ferry ride on the Elbe; regular ferries run and are cheap with a transit ticket.
Add a day trip to the Speicherstadt museums or the International Maritime Museum if you like ships.
Planten un Blomen park and the Wallanlagen are free and good for a slow half-day in dry weather.
